Thanks for the summary. Quick tech notes and proposed measurement rule set: 

- Root cause hypothesis: transient KV cache churn coupled with a maintenance-driven az-level network flap that increased tail latency for a small connection subset. Were still correlating with infra events but logs point to a brief spike in cold KV misses and retry-driven head-of-line stalls.

- Proposed temporary mitigations (immediate):
  * Route EdgeFins traffic to warm-standby pool us-west-2c for 48 hours (will need a short DNS/route change and an SNI target tag).
  * Activate the "aggressive warmup" playbook (see attached warmup_playbook-v2.pdf) to prepopulate KV caches for top 120 prompt hashes.
  * Enable model-variant fallback with quality gate: only fallback to variant q1.5 when p95 > 700ms for 5 consecutive 5-minute buckets AND output-quality checks (synthetic prompt set) pass (max top-k divergence threshold 0.02).

- Measurement exclusion rules (how Redwood will treat data):
  1) Only samples that match both (A) a timestamp within the event window and (B) request route listed in the CSV will be excluded from our canonical p95 calculation.
  2) Excluded samples will be tagged as "transient-outlier" in our audit logs and visible to both parties.
  3) Any exclusion action will be gated by a post-event joint review — we will not apply retrospective exclusions without documented samples and mutual sign-off (Marcus/EdgeFin rep).

- Duration & revert: 48 hours default; if new evidence arises we can extend to 72 hours but will require an additional sign-off. Revert plan is automatic rollback to primary pool with a 10-minute ramp and health-check gating.

I will coordinate the routing change and warmup steps. Marissa, can Legal/Contracts prepare a brief carveout addendum for signature?

Laura Bennett
Sr. Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
